agree.reason: The apology up front and the candid account of the churn would help with an investor who is already cold, but the runway section is an unfilled bracket, and that leaves this reader without the one thing they need to decide whether to keep backing the company.

honest.reason: The numbers are accurate (about 11 months of runway, about 13% of revenue, no-shows nearly halved), but 'independents are a different situation' and the claim that the standalone feature avoids competing with built-in schedulers are stated with more confidence than the brief supports.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the runway, the lost customer's share of revenue and the no-show improvement, but it never says how many $150 reminder subscriptions would cover the $44,000 monthly burn (about 290) or when cash runs out (around late 2027).

right_comparison.reason: It names the trend of records vendors bundling scheduling and the flat revenue, but it never spells out what happens if nothing changes: flat revenue until the cash runs out in about 11 months.

qualification.reason: The promise to report sign-ups next quarter has no target number and no consequence if it is missed, and the runway plan is still a placeholder.

objections.reason: It answers the missed-updates complaint directly and admits the churn is structural, but it leaves open this reader's real question: what is the plan for the 11 months of runway, and why keep funding?

fit.reason: It is under 500 words and has the right shape for an investor update, but the bracketed placeholders mean it can't be sent to the 11 investors as written.
